newsitem.title: USA: Conf Board -- consumer conf not necessarily peaked.
newsitem.headline: Conf Board -- consumer conf not necessarily peaked.

text.p: The Conference Board, a business research and membership network, said a more than three-point drop in its consumer confidence index in July is not necessarily a sign that the measure has peaked.

Ken Goldstein, senior economist at The Conference Board, told Reuters Financial Television that the decline in the overall index was a result of consumer perceptions following two "relatively weak labor reports" and questions as to how long the economic upturn can last.
Still, asked whether the downturn was a sign that consumer confidence has peaked, Goldstein replied "not necessarily."
But Goldstein said the psychological effect of the labor reports had begun to wash through the data. In addition, consumers were more dubious of a further extension of the economic recovery, he said.
"People are beginning to say this is a really good economy, but how much longer can it last," Goldstein said.

Goldstein noted jobs data from June and May were not bad reports, but certainly not "real good" reports such as those seen in March and April. With that said, he underscored the importance of July's employment report on Friday to the future of consumers' pscyhes.
